newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges dip, prompt low sulphur up.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges dip, prompt low sulphur up.

text.p: Euro high sulphur fuel barges fell on Tuesday with a trader aggressively selling stored material at lower numbers while low sulphur barges traded strong for promptish delivery, traders said.
High sulphur barges traded at $93.50 fob ARA early in the morning before an independent trading house sold at $93 a tonne some 10,000 tonnes of stored material.
Some traders also said that they heard $92.50 was done but there was no immediate confirmation.
"$93 was done several times by a trading house. They have an awful lot of product in storage and they want to sell it. They were very aggressive today with 380 (CST)," one trader said.
A second trader, asked if the seller was trying to drive the market lower, said: "No. We bid them $93 now and they won't do it. What ever they were doing they did earlier."
Prompt low sulphur fuel barges traded strong with a refiner selling at $101 fob ex-Flushing 500 tonnes to a bunker buyer in the Netherlands -- the first trade reported in the market in over a week.
"That's a small quantity for delivery the end of next week. I think the market for regular low sulphur barges is $1 or $2 lower," a trader with the refiner said.

Russian high sulphur cracked was largely steady with two cargoes on offer at two means +$2 and straight-run was unchanged also in early talk, with three E-4s carrying a price tag of about three means flat.
